review_note: Independent review confirmed a dense Laplace oracle for a structured intercept in log sigma (non-Gaussian marginal). The oracle uses only fixture quantities (ape::vcv, a supplied matrix, or a hand-built exponential kernel), its own gradient and Hessian, two oracle starts, and finite-difference checks of its derivatives. No drmTMB helper is called. It supports all 4 linked rows: native Gaussian sigma:I, identity link, with phylo(tree), animal(A=K), relmat(K) and spatial(coords), each with sd(id, level=..., dpar='sigma') ~ z. Agreement is 1e-4, with mode gradient < 1e-8, positive-definite Hessian and mode gap < 1e-6. K is stored in shuffled level order and data are shuffled. Emulated-bug sensitivity exists: a swapped SD slope, reversed SD rows and constant SD each shift the oracle by more than 1e-2, run for relmat and phylo. The oracle is provider-agnostic, so this covers the animal and spatial rows through the same function. Constant-SD limit is 1e-5, and neighbouring routes (sigma slope, mu plus sigma, ordinary+structured, meta_V, aggregation) are asserted closed. Focused test rerun on the current worktree: 92 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, 0 skipped. Manifest rehash: 2 of 5 entries differ (R/drmTMB.R, src/drmTMB.cpp). They were changed by later lane commits (386543c70, fe12743c8), so the old states could not be reproduced. The current-file rerun is the evidence. Does not establish animal Ainv or pedigree rows, relmat Q, mesh or precision-matrix rows, sigma slopes or q2, recovery, calibration, coverage or Julia parity. The receipt manifest needs a refresh.
